title: Swahili Beef Soup
community: Swahili coast — the aromatic coastal beef soup
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Swahili Supu ya Mchuzi — beef bone broth simmered with coconut milk, Zanzibar spices, and fresh herbs. The coastal version of bone soup — richer, more aromatic, and more deeply flavoured than the mainland version through the addition of coastal spices and coconut milk.
longDesc: Swahili beef soup is the coastal enrichment of the mainland bone broth — the same restorative, nourishing preparation but elevated by Zanzibar spices and a final addition of coconut milk. Given to the sick, eaten before a long journey, and served at coastal celebrations as a starter.
steps: Blanch bones 5 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Place bones, water, onion, garlic, ginger, lemon grass, and whole spices in a large pot.
Bring to a boil. Skim foam.
Simmer on lowest heat for 75—90 minutes.
Add coconut milk. Simmer gently 8 minutes.
Garnish with coriander. Serve with lime.
chefTips: The whole spices are the key coastal signature.
Add coconut milk only after straining — never boil it.
cookingScience: See TZA034 for bone broth science.
sustainabilityTips: Uses bones that would otherwise be discarded.
culturalNote: Swahili bone soup is the coastal version of Tanzania's most restorative food — given to the sick and the recovering, perfumed with the spices of the island, enriched with coconut milk.
